walkthroughs.body_html:
The UK Business Environment — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The UK Business Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The UK Business Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Porter's three generic strategies are cost leadership, differentiation and:
options: Diversification
Focus
Innovation
Acquisition

mcqs.q: The 'Blue Ocean' concept was proposed by:
options: Porter
Kim and Mauborgne
Hamel and Prahalad
Drucker
PESTLE analyses the internal strengths and weaknesses of a business.
Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.
The external macro-environment: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors affecting a business.
PESTLE stands for Profit, Earnings, Sales, Trade, Loans, Equity.
Just-in-time means delivering products to customers exactly on time.
PESTLE stands for Profit, Earnings, Sales, Trade, Loans, Equity.
Just-in-time means finishing work right before the deadline.
Holding minimal stock and receiving inputs only when needed for production — reducing storage costs but increasing vulnerability to supply disruption.
PESTLE stands for Profit, Earnings, Sales, Trade, Loans, Equity.

Competitive rivalry, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, bargaining power of suppliers, bargaining power of buyers — together determining industry attractiveness and potential profitability.
Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.
Porter's Five Forces are five business strategies a firm should choose between.
